She ran off like she was being chased and came back with the menu. She took everyone's order and finally came back around to me. I asked for the chocolate cake and specifically told her I wanted my dessert when everyone's food came out because I wanted to eat with everyone else. One of my guy friends had ordered another beer when he ordered his food but it never came out. He had to get up literally after his food came out and go up to the bar to get a beer (roughly about 30 minutes after he had ordered it). My fiancé asked for a chicken plate and ordered oysters as an appetizer. My friend also ordered the oysters as an appetizer. We waited for them to come out but our entrees came out before the appetizers. My friend, who'd ordered the oysters also had a soup, but to our surprise no one brought her a spoon. How was she supposed to eat her soup? With a fork? We finally found another server that was walking by and asked for a spoon. She said she would be back with one and completely forgot. So we grabbed another server and he brought her one. By then everyone was eating and we still didn't have the oysters, and I didn't have my dessert, so I was just eating off of my fiancé's plate. Claire came around with one order of oysters for my friend but not ours. My fiancé just said "don't worry about it, we'll try them another time". Besides he was getting full. Another one of my friends (who is vegetarian and had informed Claire about it) asked for a side of the whipped potatoes, and I asked if my dessert was coming. She said she was gonna go check on that. Later, the manager with the man bun, came around and asked if anyone had ordered an entree with whipped potatoes. No, we'd ordered just a side of whipped potatoes. Anyways, he informs Estefania that they were out, but he could replace it with a substitute that had crab in it. Umm, I thought we said she was vegetarian? He was like "yeah that wouldn't be fun." He then proceeded to ask if everything was okay. By this time everyone was done with their food (except Franchesca who was still working on her oysters that were supposed to be an appetizer), and I still didn't have my dessert. I asked him where it was and that I had asked for it to come out with everyone's food. He said they were barely working on it. What a shock. He cleared our table and dropped all the plates. (Sigh). After that was cleaned up, my dessert was finally there. I was the only one with a plate on the table now. I finished my dessert and Claire came back around. Not to our table though, to the table next to us. She kept her back towards us and wouldn't turn around even though we were calling her. As a server, I literally hate when people flag me down but we had no choice but to wave at her for her to even notice us. Being a server I know when a server is purposely ignoring their tables, and that's exactly what she was doing. We asked for the check. When she came back she was charging me for two drinks when I only had one. I then informed her that I was being charged for two drinks and goes "but you had two drinks." Ummm what? She went to our table three times throughout our entire experience, so when had I ordered that other drink? She then goes on to say "well who had two drinks?" No one, girl. Because you forgot about my friends beer! She had put one of my friend's drink in my tab. She then fixed it. Gave me back the check to sign but no pen. I'd never tipped less than 20% before but this was definitely not worthy of a tip. Of course we tipped accordingly but I feel like she didn't deserve it. I'm sure Claire is great server at some level, but not that night. She treated us like ignorant foreigners, and it showed. Definitely ruined our last night in New Orleans.

text: Natural Selection is one of my favorite stores in all of Midtown Reno. Just ask my boyfriend and he can confirm that I try to sneak a visit to this shop every time we pass by. Keep in mind that they don't open until noon, so plan your visit accordingly. Atmosphere: Walking in feels like stepping into the study of an old eccentric professor. From the ceiling hangs a variety of trailing indoor plants. The displays are filled with all manner of small complete animal skeletons, individual bones, and all kinds of other preserved animal parts (quills, teeth, alligator hands). Smaller house plants and succulents are tucked into every available corner, giving the whole shop a very wild overgrown feel to it. Animal Oddities: They have the best selection of animal bones, quills, skeletons, taxidermy, etc that I've ever seen in a shop in person. Every time I go back they have new specimens and new plants in stock. If you are interested they have a great Instagram page you can follow to stay up to date on all the new things coming in. Plants: I love how helpful the staff is here when buying a new plant. They are very knowledgeable on how to take care of each plant so that you have the best possible start.

text: I came for David Bowie art and discovered a museum that had much more than I expected! So when I learned that they were moving it to National Liberty Museum this year, and that they were going to have it on display for a full month, I decided to make a day visit out of it. And when I did I realized that the full museum featured so much more than just the kitschy never forget 9/11 things that I was expecting. Liberty is one of those subjective words that can be linked to anything from religion and science, to heroism and inspiration, to anywhere in between. And I was pleasantly surprised to see a little bit of all of those things represented within the museums confines. Outside of the obvious Bowie exhibit, I was also very won over by the wall of inspirational heroes who made an impact despite facing physical and cognitive disabilities. Another incredible room was. The Heroes From Around The World room is also noteworthy for paying homage to noteworthy people like Nelson Mandela and Anne Frank, and featuring a breathtaking Flame of Liberty installation from world renowned glass artist, Dale Chihuly. While the Bowie exhibit is long gone it gave a wonderful showing of what the museums special exhibits had to feature, while offering up some things that the previous years Bowie art installations didn't, like art from elementary and middle school students who were newly exposed to his music. While it may also invoke a grain of sadness, the latest special exhibit, Forbidden Art from the collections of the Auschwitz Memorial, may very well do the same during a time when its needed to.

text: Well, I hate to say this about a new business but this place is awful and merits this review. I went in and ordered 12 tacos and spent $33 in doing so: 4 chicken, 4 carne asada, 2 supremes, 1 brisket, and 1 lobster. I ordered to go as I live less than a mile away and waited 20 minutes for my order. The inside of the place is nice and looks clean. There is a machine that takes balls of tortilla dough and turns them into tortillas. So, imagine thinking that you are about taco pig out on freshly made tortillas filled with tender asada, chicken, and lobster. What I got was a mess. All of the tacos were ICE cold, I'm talking freezing, cold to the touch. So cold, the tortillas were almost hard in places. There was very little ingredients in each taco relative to the tortilla size and the tortillas were not freshly made but store bought. The lobster taco had so much sauce on it the tortilla was soggy but there was a adequate amount of lobster. The asada meat itself was decent but there was a large dollop of guac on one side of the taco and virtually no cheese. The chicken tacos didn't have much flavor. The Supreme tacos were probably the worst as they were filled with cold ground beef and retried beans. There is virtually no way I am coming back here. I wish I had taken more pictures but just ended up so pissed that I threw everything away. $33 in the trash.

The purpose of the box was to keep patrons socially distanced from one another. The only time either of us had stepped out of the box was to go to the restroom (with our masks on). The conversation with the manager and bouncer had become counter constructive, so I gave our bartender a $40 tip and out of frustration threatened to leave without paying. Seconds later I found myself being lifted up off the ground and smashed onto the floor. The attitude and actions of the security personnel that evening were akin to the police brutality that everyone is protesting against - unnecessary excessive force from an overzealous nut bag with too much unearned authority. So if you are in Nashville, I hope that my story can serve as a reminder of what you can expect if you step out of your little covid box one too many times. Started with dumplings and honey glazed spare ribs to share - both were so delicious. I have to admit that I like very thin skins on my dumplings, and the skins are a little on the thicker side, but not as much as most Chinese take-out places (I do not consider this to be a standard Chinese take-out, by any means). The slightly sweet ribs were perfectly seasoned. My husband also ordered soup, which he loved, but I cannot remember what he ordered. He suggested that we split an order of the Honey Walnut Shrimp, which we have previously had, both here, and at Chez Elena Wu; I told him I would not ever share this delightful dish, after looking at him as if he had gone stark raving mad! This is one of the most wonderful meals, and it has ALWAYS been made to perfection. I have tried several other entrees, but each time, I wish I had gone back to my HW Shrimp. Not that the other dishes weren't delicious, but this one is perfection. Service has always been pleasant, and efficient enough that I have no complaints. The prices are very good, especially when you are not paying the mark up on alcohol. I truly recommend Très Yan and Wu! text: This company is awful. It appears that they love to take advantage of property owners that may not live in the state and/or customers that do not understand how HVAC systems work. Today, our tenant complained that the heat stopped working in the middle of the night. Snowflake Air was contracted by our property management group to go out and diagnose the issue. They told us that our furnace was is poor shape, and that the capacitor for the motor was faulty. Furthermore, he told us that we needed to replace our computer board. When I asked why he thought it was in poor shape and what codes the computer board was throwing, the owner could not tell me anything, other than the unit is old; he just offered vague details. This repair was estimated at $1000 which included a "tune-up" (btw- any company that wants to do a "tune up" is a red flag being that there is no way to "tune up" a furnace- other than wipe down the inside of the unit and possibly clean a filter) Beyond that, they pushed at replacing the furnace with a total estimated cost at close to $6000. The only explanation given for this was that our unit was 16 years old and is almost at the end of its life. Snowflake Air claimed that they just wanted to give us options. (This reminds me of a car dealer who pushes you toward a new car because a fuse is out on your existing car.) We decided to call another local company that told us that it was just the capacitor, and that the board was fine. The total cost was $218. I asked the tech if our unit was close to the end of it's life. He told me that the unit was in great shape and that we could get at least another 10 to 15 years out of it and possibly more as long as we kept it in good condition. I see that this company has good reviews, and I will say that the representative that I spoke with was nice and friendly, but it makes me wonder how many others were taken advantage of by their appearance at being kind. Clearly, I would not recommend this company, and my advice is to always get a second opinion. In response to Snowflake Air's comments and mischaracterization of the situation is as follows: 1. I understand that you work for multiple property management companies, but that really says nothing about your character. My point is that you are able to go out to a premises where an owner may not be able to go, you are trusted to give your best opinion and a fair and honest evaluation of the issue. Clearly, you did not do this in this case, and it only leads me to assume that this type of dishonesty is the status quo- but that is a guess. As a client, I would never want to be in a situation where I have to question whether or not my vendor is honest or not. 2. I was told specifically by you that the furnace was in poor condition. When I asked why it received the poor condition label, you could not give me an answer. Furthermore, the control board was not reset. It was simply cleared of the existing codes. If there was damage, as stated by the other technician, you would see some kind of a short circuit on the back of the board. In the end, the capacitor should've been replaced first and then the board should have been tested and evaluated at that point. 3. As far as the "tune up" goes, cleaning and checking the system is not considered a tuneup. It is just considered an evaluation which should be included in any service call. The tech from the second company that we called out took care of all these items as part of his normal service fee. He did not add any charges nor did he create this bogus "tune up" term. 4. I understand now that the $6000 was for both units, but this was not made clear by you or by our management company. With that being said, neither one of those units needed to be replaced. When you bring up a needless argument to replace $6000 worth of equipment, your statements that some owners like to do this only leads me to believe that you have pushed them into replacing units that do not need to be replaced. 5. As far as your professionalism goes, I would argue that wall friendly, you like a true professional lens into what needs to be serviced and what does not. It is clear that you live convinced others to replace things that do not need to be replaced. In the end, everyone has to make up their own mind who to hire. I just want to lay out the facts for others who are looking for a reputable company. This company, for now, is not a reputable company in my opinion. text: The day before Thanksgiving my family decided to check out the recently opened Harps of Trinity Irish Pub and Grill and we certainly were not disappointed. There is a mix of high-top and low tables which are nicely buffered by well-placed planters. We were happy to see some familiar faces like owner Vince La Mattina and our favorite bartender Taylor. Manager Masahiko also stopped by as he made his rounds to ensure everyone was being well taken care of. Our waiter Hunter was knowledgeable and attentive but allowed us to relax and enjoy our experience which we absolutely did. Thanks for excellent service Hunter! The vibe of Harps was impressive but the true star of the night was the amazing cuisine prepared by Chef Rob and his incredibly talented kitchen staff. Our daughter ordered the Fish and Chips which we all had to try. The fish was properly battered and crisp on the outside yet tender and moist on the inside. It was obvious the fries were fresh cut and again, cooked perfectly. This was also accompanied by a tasty homemade coleslaw and is a dish I would certainly recommend. My wife and I decided to try the entrée special that night which was Grilled Mahi Mahi with Shishito Coconut Rice, house veggies and green coconut sauce. We were both impressed on how beautifully the food was arranged on our plates. The Mahi was grilled to perfection and extremely tasty and moist. The shishito coconut rice was bursting with flavor and was the perfect accompaniment for the fish as was the green coconut sauce for dipping. This was paired with a mélange of delicious roasted and seasoned zucchini, yellow squash, sweet red onions and red bell pepper. And if that was not enough the fish was topped with tempura asparagus. Wow! The flavor profiles all played together nicely and when paired with The Other West Coast IPA from local Trinity brewer The Escape Brewing Company. Truly an impressive meal! Harps menu has a nice variety of appetizers, salads and entrees to please all palates. They also have live music on the weekend but even on this Wednesday night they had a DJ coming in at 9pm to kick off the Thanksgiving holiday. Harps is a welcome addition to the Trinity area and one I am sure many will come to enjoy now and in the future.
